title: Dashboard: header Loop ghosts/repeats ~20x on tmux pane reflow (Ink repaint bug)
description:
COSMETIC-ONLY TUI bug (no loop-correctness impact). The dashboard summary section heading "Loop" (src/ui/Dashboard.tsx:381, heading="Loop", gapTop=0 so it is the first line of the frame) ghosts and stacks ~20 orphaned copies above the live frame.

ROOT CAUSE (not a data/label bug; the event feed and Recent panel render correctly): Inks in-place repaint tracks the previous frames line count at the OLD terminal width. When cam-runs window-resized hook reflows the column (tmux pane resize / SIGWINCH bursts), that count is stale and the top line (the "Loop" header) is left ghosted. The code already documents this exact failure mode at src/commands/dashboard.ts:948-957 and 1030-1039.

WHY THE CURRENT MITIGATION MISSES IT: makeResizeClearer (src/commands/dashboard.ts:970-1005) only writes a clear on the resize event. The poll-driven re-render (src/ui/Dashboard.tsx:144-149, fires every poll interval) repaints with NO clear at all. So a poll repaint at a stale height, or a tmux pane resize that never surfaces as a process.stdout resize event inside the pane, leaves the ghosts stacked.

CANDIDATE FIX (spec later, do not implement from this issue): add a clear/repaint-reset to the poll-driven re-render path, or force a full-frame clear when the rendered height changes, not only on the resize event. Verify against a real tmux pane reflow, not a fake.

Evidence: operator screenshot 2026-07-15 showing ~20 Loop rows above the state/story/progress block.

spec.scope: Fix the cosmetic 'Loop' header ghosting on tmux pane reflow by adding a width-change-detected clear to the dashboard's poll-driven re-render path (src/ui/Dashboard.tsx:144-149). Track the column width used at the last paint; when the poll re-render sees a different stdout.columns, write a full-frame clear (CURSOR.clear) before the repaint. Keep the existing makeResizeClearer resize-event path. Cosmetic-only; no loop-correctness impact. Out of scope: a requires:operator visual ceremony -- the operator elected deterministic-test-only verification (the real-tmux visual is an informal post-ship eyeball, non-blocking).
acceptanceCriteria: The dashboard tracks the column width (stdout.columns) used at the last paint; on the poll-driven re-render (Dashboard.tsx:144-149), when the current width differs from the last-paint width, a full-frame clear (CURSOR.clear, the \x1b[H\x1b[J escape) is written before the repaint.
In steady state (width unchanged between poll ticks), no clear is written on the poll path -- zero flicker.
The existing makeResizeClearer resize-event clear path (src/commands/dashboard.ts:970-1005) is preserved as belt-and-suspenders.

A deterministic unit test drives a column-width change between poll ticks via an injectable seam and asserts a clear is written exactly when the width changed and NOT when the width is unchanged, using the existing fake writeFn/stdout pattern (no real tmux).
Verification: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test`, and `bun run check:all` are green.
gotchas: Root cause is column reflow invalidating Ink's internal (stale) previous-frame line-count; key the detection on WIDTH (stdout.columns), not height. There is no app-side line-count to compare against -- last-paint width tracking is a new addition.
CURSOR.clear is defined at src/commands/dashboard.ts:64 as "\x1b[H\x1b[J" (home cursor + clear-to-end). Reuse it, do not hand-roll a new escape.

The poll path lives inside the React component (setInterval -> setData at Dashboard.tsx:144-149); writing a raw escape from the component is a layering smell. Source width from useStdout()/an injected stdout and keep the seam injectable so the unit test can drive a width change deterministically.

Existing tests (test/dashboard.test.ts:899-990) fake writeFn + a fake clock and assert what makeResizeClearer WRITES, not whether a ghost occurs; the new test similarly asserts the escape is written on width-change -- the deterministic proxy the operator accepted in lieu of a CI visual confirmation.

The render instance (Ink) is used only for waitUntilExit(); instance.clear()/rerender/patchConsole are available but unused -- staying with raw CURSOR.clear escapes matches the existing resize path and avoids a broader refactor.
